svg.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Measure and improve, with the firewall
svg.desc: Two boxes at the top hold the two kinds of material a scorer may say it reads. On the left, in blue, what is written before any opening of held-out data: the request, the plan as locked, the tests on known answers, the log up to the lock, an exploration's log and lead, and a review recorded before any opening. On the right, in red, what is written from the first opening on: what an opening of real held-out data showed, the finding and the review of it, and the log from the opening on. Below the left box, judge scorers (a rubric, a model, one label) read only the left box. Below the right box, deterministic scorers (a named check the study tool works out) read both boxes. A vertical bar between the two columns is the firewall: two dashed lines from the right column end at it, with the words no judge reads past this line, the validator refuses it. On the left, below the judges, a proposal to change the definition is fed only by scorers marked selfImprovement true; the loop that would make one is not built. On the right, what the deterministic scorers find is counted and shown to people, with selfImprovement false, and what an opening showed also feeds the knowledge loop as notes and drafted pages that a person signs. At the bottom, a proposal is tested on benchmarks: blind cases with a planted, sealed truth, never real held-out data, in a design set kept as files and an acceptance set generated from a seed kept outside, under two versions of the definition. From there, in amber, a person adopts a change, with its prediction in the change log.
